questions.question: If four resistances of 4 ohm each are connected in parallel, what will be their effective resistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 ohm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When resistors are connected in parallel, the total or effective resistance (Rₜₒₜₐₗ) decreases.
 
• The formula for the total resistance of resistors in parallel is given by 1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ + 1/R₄.
 
• For four resistors of 4 ohms each in parallel, the calculation is: 1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 4/4.
 
• Thus, Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1 ohm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Series vs Parallel Circuits:**

 
 
• In series circuits, resistors are connected end-to-end, resulting in an increase in total resistance.
 
• In parallel circuits, resistors are connected across the same two points, resulting in a decrease in total resistance.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that V = IR, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
• This law is fundamental in analyzing electrical circuits.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Parallel Circuits:**
 
 
• Used in household electrical wiring to ensure that appliances can operate independently.
 
• Common in electronic devices where components need to operate at the same voltage.
 
 
 
• **Resistor Ratings:**
 
 
• Resistors are rated based on their resistance value (in ohms) and their power rating (in watts).
 
• It is important to choose resistors with appropriate ratings to prevent overheating and damage.

questions.question: Bhavnath Mahadev fair is held every year in which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Junagarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhavnath Mahadev Fair is an annual event held in **Junagarh, Gujarat**.
 
• This fair takes place at the **Bhavnath Mahadev Temple**, located at the foothills of the Girnar mountain.
 
• The fair is celebrated during the **Mahashivratri** festival, which usually falls in February or March.
 
• It attracts a large number of devotees, including the **Naga Sadhus**, who come to take a holy dip in the Mrigi Kund.
 
• The event features various cultural programs, religious rituals, and a procession of decorated elephants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Girnar Mountain:**

 
 
• Girnar is a collection of mountains in the Junagadh District of Gujarat, India.
 
• It is considered a sacred site for both Hindus and Jains.
 
• The mountain hosts a number of temples, the most significant being the Neminath Temple and the Amba Mata Temple.
 
 
 
• **Mahashivratri Festival:**
 
 
• Mahashivratri is a Hindu festival celebrated annually in honor of Lord Shiva.
 
• It signifies the convergence of divine powers and the end of darkness and ignorance.
 
• Devotees observe fasting, chanting, and night-long vigils during this festival.
 
 
 
• **Naga Sadhus:**
 
 
• Naga Sadhus are a sect of Hindu ascetics who renounce all material possessions.
 
• They are known for their austere lifestyle and participation in religious events like the Kumbh Mela.
 
• They usually remain unclothed and cover their bodies with ash.
 
 
 
• **Mrigi Kund:**
 
 
• Mrigi Kund is a sacred water tank located near the Bhavnath Mahadev Temple.
 
• It is believed that a dip in this tank during the Bhavnath Fair purifies the soul.
 
• The tank is also associated with various religious legends and myths.

questions.question: As per the 2001 Census, what is the specific age, for a person to be called literate?

• **Importance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Literacy is vital for social and economic development.
 
• It empowers individuals and improves quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Programs in India:**
 
 
• Numerous government initiatives aim to improve literacy rates, such as the National Literacy Mission.

questions.question: A section of an active fault that has produced earthquakes in the past but is now quiet and is believed that the fault segment is capable of producing earthquake on some other basis is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seismic Gap**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A seismic gap is a section of an active fault that has not experienced a recent earthquake but is believed to be capable of producing one based on historical seismic activity.
 
• This concept is used in earthquake prediction models to identify areas that may be at higher risk of future earthquakes.
 
• Seismic gaps are identified by comparing the timing and magnitude of past earthquakes along a fault line.
 
• Regions identified as seismic gaps often undergo detailed monitoring to better understand the potential for future seismic activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypocenter:** The point within the Earth where an earthquake rupture starts. It is located beneath the Earth's surface.
 
• **Epicenter:** The point on the Earth's surface directly above the hypocenter. It is the location where the earthquake is felt most strongly.
 
• **Seismic Waves:** Waves of energy that travel through the Earth as a result of an earthquake. These include primary (P) waves, secondary (S) waves, and surface waves.
 
• **Active Fault:** A fault that has had recent movements and is expected to produce earthquakes in the future. These faults are often the focus of seismic hazard assessments.

questions.question: When was the Wildlife Protection Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1972**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Wildlife Protection Act was enacted by the Indian Parliament in **1972**.
 
• The Act provides for the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants and matters connected with them, with a view to ensuring the ecological and environmental security of India.
 
• The Act includes provisions for the creation of protected areas such as national parks and wildlife sanctuaries to conserve wildlife.
 
• It also regulates hunting, trade, and commerce in wild animals, animal products, and trophies.
 
• The Act has been amended multiple times to make the protection measures more stringent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries:**

 
 
• India has over 100 national parks and more than 500 wildlife sanctuaries.
 
• Kanha National Park, Jim Corbett National Park, and Kaziranga National Park are some of the prominent ones.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched in 1973, Project Tiger is a major wildlife conservation initiative.
 
• It aims to protect tigers and their habitats.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Reserves:**
 
 
• These are designated areas that act as buffer zones between established protected areas and human settlements.
 
• They help in maintaining the ecological balance.
 
 
 
• **Important Amendments:**
 
 
• The Act has been amended in 1982, 1986, 1991, 2002, and 2006 to strengthen the legal framework for wildlife protection.
 
• The 2002 Amendment led to the establishment of the National Board for Wildlife.

questions.question: The Mahananda River rising in the _____ is a tributary of Ganga.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Darjeeling Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mahananda River originates from the **Darjeeling Hills** in the Indian state of West Bengal.
 
• It flows through the states of West Bengal and Bihar in India and also through parts of Bangladesh.
 
• The river ultimately joins the Ganga River near the town of **Godagari in Bangladesh**.
 
• The Mahananda River plays a crucial role in irrigation and agriculture in the regions it traverses.
 
• This river is part of the larger Ganga Basin, which is one of the most important river basins in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Darjeeling Hills:**

 
 
• Located in the eastern Himalayas, Darjeeling is known for its stunning vistas, tea gardens, and colonial architecture.
 
• The region is famous for the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• It has a diverse range of flora and fauna, owing to its varying altitudes and climate.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River Basin:**
 
 
• The Ganga Basin is the most fertile and densely populated river basin in the world.
 
• It supports a population of around 400 million people in India.
 
• The Ganga River is considered sacred in Hinduism and is a lifeline for millions of people.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation and Agriculture:**
 
 
• Rivers like the Mahananda are crucial for irrigation in the agricultural sectors of West Bengal and Bihar.
 
• The river's water is used to grow crops such as rice, wheat, and sugarcane.
 
 
 
• **Tributaries of the Ganga:**
 
 
• The Ganga has numerous tributaries, including the Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi rivers.
 
• These tributaries play a vital role in maintaining the flow and health of the Ganga River.

questions.question: Which of the following is a traditional game of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kabbadi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kabbadi** is a traditional team sport that originated in ancient India.
 
• The game is a combination of wrestling and tag, and it is primarily popular in rural areas of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Kabbadi is recognized as the national sport of Bangladesh and is also played extensively in countries like Nepal, Pakistan, and Iran.
 
• The sport is governed by the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF) and is included in the Asian Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basic Rules:**

 
 
• The game is played between two teams of seven players each, with each match consisting of two 20-minute halves.
 
• The objective is for a single player, known as a "raider," to tag members of the opposing team and return to their half without being tackled.
 
 
 
• **Types of Kabaddi:**
 
 
• There are different forms of kabaddi such as Sanjeevani, Gaminee, and Amar.
 
• The most popular format in international competitions is the standard style, which is played on a rectangular court.
 
 
 
• **Popularity:**
 
 
• Kabaddi has gained international popularity through leagues such as the Pro Kabaddi League in India.
 
• The sport is also part of school curriculums and local tournaments across India.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Kabaddi is believed to have been practiced as a form of physical exercise and recreation in ancient India.
 
• The game has cultural and historical significance, often associated with the Mahabharata and other Indian epics.

questions.question: A group of natural substances with variable phenolic structures, which are found in fruits, vegetables, and grains is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flavonoids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Flavonoids are a diverse group of phytonutrients found in almost all fruits and vegetables.
 
• These compounds are known for their antioxidant properties and play a crucial role in protecting the body against various diseases.
 
• Flavonoids are responsible for the vibrant colors of many fruits and vegetables.
 
• They have been linked to numerous health benefits including improved heart health, reduced inflammation, and enhanced immune function.
 
• Common dietary sources of flavonoids include apples, berries, onions, tea, and dark chocolate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Flavonoids:**

 
 
• Flavonols: Found in onions, kale, and broccoli.
 
• Flavan-3-ols: Present in tea, grapes, and cocoa.
 
• Anthocyanins: Provide red, purple, and blue colors to berries.
 
 
 
• **Antioxidant Properties:** Flavonoids help neutralize harmful free radicals in the body, reducing oxidative stress and preventing cell damage.
 
• **Anti-Inflammatory Effects:** These compounds can inhibit the production of pro-inflammatory molecules, thus aiding in the reduction of inflammation.
 
• **Cardiovascular Health:** Regular consumption of flavonoid-rich foods is associated with lower blood pressure, improved cholesterol levels, and reduced risk of heart disease.
 
• **Potential Cancer Prevention:** Some studies suggest that flavonoids may help in protecting against certain types of cancer by inhibiting tumor growth and promoting apoptosis in cancer cells.

questions.question: The Moplah Uprising, an organised opposition of Muslim cultivators, occurred in which modern state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Moplah Uprising, also known as the Mappila Rebellion, occurred in the Malabar region of Kerala in 1921.
 
• This rebellion was led by the Mappila Muslims of Kerala, who were primarily tenants and cultivators.
 
• The uprising was a reaction against British colonial rule and the oppressive practices of landlords.
 
• The rebellion saw widespread violence and was one of the significant peasant movements in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• It was part of the larger Khilafat Movement and Non-Cooperation Movement against British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khilafat Movement:**

 
 
• A pan-Islamist political campaign launched by Muslims in British India to influence the British government not to abolish the Ottoman Caliphate.
 
• It was led by prominent Muslim leaders like Maulana Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**
 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, this was a mass protest against British rule.
 
• It aimed at inducing the British government to grant self-governance to India.
 
 
 
• **Malabar Region:**
 
 
• Located in the northern part of Kerala, the Malabar region was historically significant due to its trading ports.
 
• It was a major center for the spice trade and saw various foreign influences over centuries.
 
 
 
• **Tenant Farming:**
 
 
• A system where farmers cultivate land owned by another and pay rent in the form of cash or a portion of the produce.
 
• In the Malabar region, the oppressive practices by landlords led to widespread discontent among tenant farmers.

questions.question: What is the major purpose of the Salal Dam located on Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydroelectricity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Salal Dam, also known as Salal Hydroelectric Power Station, is primarily used for generating hydroelectric power.
 
• It is located on the Chenab River in the Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir, India.
 
• The dam has an installed capacity of 690 megawatts, providing significant power to the region.
 
• The construction of the Salal Dam was completed in two stages, with Stage I completed in 1987 and Stage II in 1995.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chenab River:**

 
 
• The Chenab River is one of the major rivers in the Indian subcontinent, flowing through India and Pakistan.
 
• It originates from the confluence of the Chandra and Bhaga rivers in the Lahaul and Spiti districts of Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• The river is a key source of irrigation and hydroelectric power in the region.
 
 
 
• **Hydroelectric Power:**
 
 
• Hydroelectric power is generated by using the energy of flowing water to turn turbines connected to generators.
 
• It is a renewable and clean source of energy, contributing significantly to reducing carbon emissions.
 
• Hydroelectric power plants can provide reliable and consistent power supply, especially in regions with abundant water resources.
 
 
 
• **Reasi District:**
 
 
• Reasi is a district in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, known for its scenic beauty and religious significance.
 
• The district is home to several important hydropower projects, including the Salal Dam.
 
• Reasi is also a popular tourist destination, attracting visitors to places like Vaishno Devi and Shiv Khori.
 
 
 
• **Energy Infrastructure in Jammu and Kashmir:**
 
 
• Jammu and Kashmir have several hydroelectric projects, contributing significantly to the region's power supply.
 
• These projects are crucial for meeting the energy demands of the area and for economic development.
 
• The region's topography and water resources make it an ideal location for hydroelectric power generation.

questions.question: Who amongst the following stated the Grameen model of microfinance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prof. Muhammad Yunus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Prof. Muhammad Yunus is the founder of the Grameen Bank and is credited with developing the Grameen model of microfinance.
 
• The Grameen model focuses on providing microloans to the impoverished without requiring collateral.
 
• This model has been instrumental in lifting millions out of poverty, particularly in rural Bangladesh.
 
• Prof. Yunus was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 for his efforts through the Grameen Bank to create economic and social development from below.
 
• The Grameen model has inspired similar microfinance institutions worldwide, promoting financial inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance:**

 
 
• Microfinance is a type of banking service provided to unemployed or low-income individuals who otherwise would not have access to financial services.
 
• It includes microloans, savings, insurance, and payment systems.
 
• Microfinance aims to support entrepreneurship and alleviate poverty.
 
 
 
• **Grameen Bank:**
 
 
• Established in 1983 by Prof. Muhammad Yunus in Bangladesh.
 
• The bank operates on the principle of trust, offering small loans to the impoverished without requiring collateral.
 
• It primarily targets women, who constitute about 97% of its borrowers.
 
 
 
• **Nobel Peace Prize 2006:**
 
 
• Prof. Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank jointly won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.
 
• The prize recognized their efforts to create economic and social development from below.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion:**
 
 
• Financial inclusion refers to efforts to make financial products and services accessible and affordable to all individuals and businesses, regardless of their net worth or size.
 
• It is a key driver for reducing poverty and boosting prosperity.

questions.question: In February 2023, there have been protests in Punjab to release a group of Sikh prisoners who have been in jail for more than 30 years since militancy was wiped out in Punjab in the 1990s. What are these prisoners called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bandi Singhs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bandi Singhs is a term used to refer to Sikh prisoners who have been jailed for a long duration, specifically those who were imprisoned during the period of militancy in Punjab in the 1980s and 1990s.
 
• In February 2023, there were significant protests in Punjab demanding the release of these prisoners, as many have been incarcerated for over 30 years.
 
• The term "Bandi Singhs" translates to "Imprisoned Sikhs" in English.
 
• The protests highlight the ongoing tensions and demands for justice and human rights for those who have been imprisoned for extended periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikh Militancy in Punjab:** The period of militancy in Punjab during the 1980s and early 1990s was marked by a violent insurgency seeking an independent Sikh state, called Khalistan.
 
• **Operation Blue Star:** A military operation carried out in June 1984 to remove Sikh militants who were amassing weapons in the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
 
• **Human Rights Concerns:** The long-term imprisonment of individuals involved in the militancy has raised significant human rights concerns, including calls for fair trials and justice.
 
• **Political Impact:** The issue of Bandi Singhs continues to have a substantial political impact in Punjab, influencing public opinion and electoral politics.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The legal framework involving the imprisonment of these individuals often includes charges under the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act (TADA), which has been criticized for its stringent provisions.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book called 'Beneath the Surface: My Story'?

• Phelps published his autobiography, **'Beneath the Surface: My Story'**, which gives an insight into his life and career.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The state religion of Bangladesh is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Islam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Islam** is the state religion of Bangladesh, as declared in the Constitution of Bangladesh.
 
• According to the 2011 census, **over 90% of the population** in Bangladesh practices Islam.
 
• Islam was declared the state religion in the **8th amendment** of the Constitution in **1988**.
 
• Muslims in Bangladesh predominantly follow the **Sunni** branch of Islam.
 
• Islamic holidays like Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha are national holidays in Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secularism in Bangladesh:**

 
 
• Despite Islam being the state religion, Bangladesh is constitutionally a secular country.
 
• The Constitution assures the right to practice other religions freely.
 
 
 
• **Religious Minorities:**
 
 
• Hinduism is the second-largest religion in Bangladesh, followed by Buddhism and Christianity.
 
• Minority religions have their own festivals and places of worship.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Before the partition of India in 1947, the region had a significant Hindu population.
 
• Post-independence from Pakistan in 1971, Bangladesh retained a significant Muslim identity.
 
 
 
• **Islamic Culture:**
 
 
• Islamic culture deeply influences the social and cultural fabric of Bangladesh.
 
• Islamic education and institutions play a significant role in society.

questions.question: Which of the following was authored by Harisenacharya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihatkatha Kosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brihatkatha Kosh** was authored by Harisenacharya.
 
• The work is significant in the genre of Sanskrit literature.
 
• It is considered one of the important texts in classical Indian narratives.
 
• Harisenacharya's contribution through this work provides insights into the cultural and social aspects of his time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajatarangini**

 
 
• Authored by Kalhana, it is a historical chronicle of the north-western Indian subcontinent, particularly the kings of Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Brihat Katha Manjari**
 
 
• Written by Kshemendra, it is an abridged version of the Brihatkatha, a large collection of stories attributed to Gunadhya.
 
 
 
• **Lilavati**
 
 
• A treatise on mathematics written by the Indian mathematician Bhaskara II, which deals with arithmetic, algebra, and geometry.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit Literature**
 
 
• Is one of the oldest literatures in the world, consisting of a vast body of texts in the Sanskrit language.
 
• Includes a wide range of works such as epics, hymns, philosophical treatises, poetry, drama, and scientific texts.
 
• Important texts include the Vedas, Upanishads, Mahabharata, Ramayana, and various other Shastras.

questions.question: Which among the following is considered the first experiment of Satyagraha by Gandhiji in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha was the first Satyagraha movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in India.
 
• It took place in 1917 in the Champaran district of Bihar.
 
• The movement was aimed at addressing the grievances of indigo farmers who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions by British planters.
 
• Gandhiji employed non-violent civil disobedience and mobilized the local peasants to protest against the exploitative system.
 
• This movement marked the beginning of Gandhiji's active involvement in the Indian independence struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indigo Cultivation**:

 
 
• Indigo was a significant cash crop during British rule, primarily used for dyeing textiles.
 
• Farmers were coerced into growing indigo on a portion of their land, often leading to severe financial losses and indebtedness.
 
 
 
• **Non-Violent Resistance**:
 
 
• Gandhiji's strategy of non-violent resistance, also known as Satyagraha, was based on the principles of truth and non-violence.
 
• This approach aimed to bring about social and political change through peaceful means.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Champaran Satyagraha**:
 
 
• The success of the Champaran Satyagraha boosted the confidence of Indian farmers and peasants in the effectiveness of non-violent protest.
 
• It also helped in highlighting the plight of the indigo farmers at a national level, garnering support for their cause.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Movements**:
 
 
• Following the Champaran Satyagraha, Gandhiji led several other significant movements like the Kheda Satyagraha, Ahmedabad Mill Strike, and the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
• These movements played crucial roles in India's fight for independence from British rule.

questions.question: Who became the first folk artist from India to walk the Cannes red carpet in 2022?

• His participation highlighted the rich cultural heritage of India on a global platform like Cannes.
 
• Mame Khan has previously contributed to several Bollywood soundtracks and international music festivals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It showcases new films of all genres, including documentaries, from around the world.
 
• It was founded in 1946 and is known for its Palme d'Or award.

• **Bollywood Contributions:**

• **International Recognition:**
 
 
• In addition to Cannes, Mame Khan has performed at various international music festivals.
 
• His work has helped promote Rajasthani folk music on global stages.

questions.question: Sonal Mansingh is a famous proponent of which of the following dance forms?

__
 
• Sonal Mansingh is one of the most renowned proponents of Odissi dance, a classical dance form from the state of Odisha, India.
 
• She has been instrumental in bringing Odissi dance to the forefront of the Indian classical dance scene.
 
• Her performances are noted for their expressive storytelling, intricate footwork, and deep emotional connect.
 
• Sonal Mansingh has received numerous awards and accolades for her contributions to Indian dance, including the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance:**

 
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest surviving dance forms of India, with origins tracing back to the temples of Odisha in eastern India.
 
• The dance form is characterized by its fluid movements, graceful gestures, and elaborate costumes.
 
• Odissi traditionally depicts religious stories and spiritual ideas, particularly related to the Hindu deities Krishna and Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Sonal Mansingh:**
 
 
• Besides Odissi, she is also well-versed in Bharatnatyam, another classical Indian dance form.
 
• She founded the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CICD) in New Delhi to promote and teach Indian classical dance.

• **Recognition and Awards:**

• She was nominated to the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of India's Parliament, in 2018.
 
 
 
• **Odissi Dance Terminologies:**
 
 
• Chauka: A basic stance in Odissi representing Lord Jagannath.
 
• Tribhangi: A posture that divides the body into three bends, a hallmark of Odissi dance.

questions.question: The union list from the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution consists of how many subjects as of May 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hundred**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union List is one of the three lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution that outlines the subjects on which the Union Government has exclusive powers to legislate.
 
• As of May 2024, the Union List consists of 100 subjects.
 
• These subjects include areas like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• The Union List is specified in Article 246 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Any subject not mentioned in the Union List, State List, or Concurrent List falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Union Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seventh Schedule:**

 
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides the powers and functions between the Union and State governments through three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
 
 
• **State List:**
 
 
• The State List contains subjects on which only the state governments can legislate. As of May 2024, it consists of 61 subjects.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• The Concurrent List includes subjects on which both the Union and State governments can legislate. It contains 52 subjects as of May 2024.
 
 
 
• **Article 246:**
 
 
• Article 246 of the Indian Constitution defines the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States. It describes the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
 
 
• **Residuary Powers:**
 
 
• Any subject not enumerated in any of the three lists falls under the residuary powers, which are exclusively with the Union Government as per Article 248.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Viharas is/are correct?

a) Viharas consist of a verandas, cell and hall around the walls of the hall.

b) Ajanta cave and Nashik cave are important parts of Vihara architecture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2) Both a and b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Viharas were ancient Buddhist monasteries consisting of a central hall, verandas, and cells for monks, typically arranged around the walls of the hall.
 
• Ajanta and Nashik caves are notable examples of Vihara architecture, showcasing intricate carvings and paintings.
 
• Viharas served as both residential and religious centers for Buddhist monks, facilitating meditation and learning.
 
• These structures were often rock-cut and found in regions like Maharashtra, demonstrating advanced ancient Indian rock-cut architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rock-cut Architecture:** This refers to structures carved directly into natural rock formations, a prominent feature in ancient Indian architecture.
 
• **Ajanta Caves:** Located in Maharashtra, these caves are famous for their exquisite murals and sculptures depicting Buddhist themes.
 
• **Nashik Caves:** Also known as Pandavleni Caves, these are a group of 24 caves carved between the 2nd century BCE and the 6th century CE, reflecting significant Buddhist influence.
 
• **Buddhist Monastic Life:** Monks resided in Viharas, where they engaged in religious study, meditation, and communal living, adhering to strict monastic codes.
 
• **Historical Significance:** Viharas played a crucial role in the spread of Buddhism, serving as centers of learning and pilgrimage during ancient times.

questions.question: Which of the following phyla contains Leech?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: Annelida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leeches belong to the phylum **Annelida**, which is characterized by segmented bodies.
 
• Annelids, commonly known as segmented worms, include earthworms, leeches, and polychaetes.
 
• Leeches are mostly found in freshwater environments, though some species live in terrestrial and marine habitats.
 
• The class Hirudinea includes leeches, which are known for their use in medicine, particularly for their anticoagulant properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phylum Annelida**:

 
 
• Annelida is a large phylum of segmented worms, which includes approximately 17,000 species.
 
• Annelids have bilateral symmetry and a true coelom (body cavity).
 
• They possess a hydrostatic skeleton that aids in movement and flexibility.
 
 
 
• **Leech Anatomy**:
 
 
• Leeches have a flattened body with 34 segments.
 
• They possess two suckers, one at each end of their body, used for attachment and movement.
 
• Many leeches have specialized structures for feeding, including jaws and pharyngeal glands.
 
 
 
• **Medical Use of Leeches**:
 
 
• Leeches have been used in medicine for centuries, primarily for bloodletting and to stimulate circulation.
 
• Their saliva contains anticoagulants, anesthetics, and vasodilators, making them useful in modern microsurgery and reconstructive surgery.
 
 
 
• **Reproduction in Annelids**:
 
 
• Most annelids reproduce sexually, and some species are hermaphroditic (possessing both male and female reproductive organs).
 
• Leeches typically lay eggs in cocoons, which are deposited in the environment.
